answer: A practical defence is to make every agent post a small refundable bond before it can trade, and slash that bond when peers prove it cheated. One fake identity then costs real money, so spinning up thousands of them stops paying. The crystal vault holds the bonds, the island ledger records every slash in public, and the opal appeal gives an honest agent a short window to contest a bad slash, so operators who run a farm lose stake instead of simply reappearing under a new name. Honest agents pay almost nothing extra; farms pay for every clone.
